correctness.rationale: The frozen baseline is a hyperbolic coexistence sink with prey-layer unstable root w and extinction sink; fixed fast-scaled shock keeps predator v=v0+O(epsilon). The scalar shock fold F(phi)=v0 gives the amplitude boundary; for larger amplitudes the unique transit time to w is precisely the positive integral. Normal hyperbolicity and compact separation from w imply post-restoration convergence to the correct sink for sufficiently small epsilon and fixed s unequal to the threshold. Differentiation proves strict monotonicity, and interior quadratic rescaling yields the exact inverse-square-root coefficient. Symbolic exact example and high-precision checks were executed; they supplement, rather than replace, analytic proof. The threshold equality and joint limits remain unproved.

value.rationale: Temporary habitat shocks differ from persistent ramps, and an exact critical duration matters for irreversible loss despite full habitat restoration. This theorem gives the complete admissible fast-pulse survival/extinction diagram across a continuum of baseline and shock parameters, identifies a sharp baseline immunity band, and computes the quantitative square-root bottleneck coefficient. It is a natural resilience boundary rather than an arbitrary special numerical case. Its illustrative shock outcome is exact, and unproved broader ecological generality is not asserted.
